words.def: A trip from one place to another, especially over a long distance.
words.example: The journey from London to Edinburgh takes about four hours by train.

words.def: To take something from someone with the intention of giving it back later.
words.example: Can I borrow your pen for a moment?

words.def: To ask someone to come to an event, such as a party or a meal.
words.example: She invited all her classmates to her birthday party.

words.def: Having a very good taste or smell.
words.example: The soup was delicious, so I asked for a second bowl.

words.def: Likely to cause harm or injury.
words.example: It is dangerous to swim in the river after heavy rain.

words.def: Behaving in a way that is respectful and considerate towards other people.
words.example: It is polite to say thank you when someone helps you.

words.def: A person who lives next to you or very near you.
words.example: Our neighbour waters our plants when we are on holiday.

words.def: An activity that you enjoy doing in your free time.
words.example: My favourite hobby is photographing old buildings.

words.def: The bags and suitcases that you take with you when you travel.
words.example: Please keep your luggage with you at all times in the station.

words.def: A piece of paper or an electronic document that shows you have paid to enter a place or to travel.
words.example: I bought two tickets for the evening concert.

words.def: Unhappy because you have no friends or people to talk to.
words.example: She felt lonely during her first month in a new city.

words.def: A person who visits a place for pleasure and to see interesting things.
words.example: The square is full of tourists taking photographs.

words.def: To succeed in doing something good, usually after a lot of effort.
words.example: He worked hard for years to achieve his dream of becoming a doctor.

words.def: Something that you do regularly, often without thinking about it.
words.example: Checking my phone first thing in the morning has become a bad habit.

words.def: A chance to do something that you want to do.
words.example: Living abroad gave her the opportunity to learn a new language.

words.def: The natural world, including air, water, land, plants and animals.
words.example: Using less plastic is good for the environment.

words.def: To tell someone that something is good or suitable for them.
words.example: Can you recommend a good restaurant near the station?

words.def: Sad because something was not as good as you hoped or expected.
words.example: I was disappointed that the film ended so suddenly.

words.def: To say that you are not satisfied with something.
words.example: Customers complained about the long waiting time.

words.def: To stay away from something or someone, or to stop something from happening.
words.example: We took a side road to avoid the traffic.

words.def: To say what you think will happen in the future.
words.example: Nobody could predict how quickly the weather would change.

words.def: Telling the truth and not likely to cheat or steal.
words.example: Thank you for being honest with me about the problem.

words.def: To help or encourage someone, especially when they are in a difficult situation.
words.example: My family supported me when I decided to change careers.

words.def: To suddenly understand or notice something.
words.example: I realised I had left my keys at the office when I reached the door.

words.def: Something or someone that you can trust to work well or behave as expected.
words.example: My car is very reliable, so I rarely have problems with it.

words.def: Not willing to do something and therefore slow to do it.
words.example: He was reluctant to speak in public because he felt nervous.

words.def: To make someone believe something or agree to do something.
words.example: She convinced her manager to try a new way of working.

words.def: To succeed in dealing with a problem or a difficult feeling.
words.example: He overcame his fear of flying by taking a short course.

words.def: Real and honest, not false or pretended.
words.example: Her smile was genuine, and everyone could see she was happy.

words.def: Working well without wasting time, money or effort.
words.example: The new system is much more efficient than the old paper forms.

words.def: Facts or signs that show that something is true.
words.example: There is strong evidence that regular exercise improves sleep.

words.def: A result of something that happened earlier, often an unpleasant one.
words.example: Missing the deadline had serious consequences for the whole team.

words.def: Able to change or be changed easily to suit new situations.
words.example: I work flexible hours, so I can start late if I need to.

words.def: To try very hard to do something that is difficult.
words.example: Many students struggle to focus when it is noisy.

words.def: Worried and nervous about something that might happen.
words.example: He felt anxious before his job interview.

words.def: To make a rough guess of an amount, cost or value.
words.example: The builders estimate that the repairs will take about three weeks.

words.def: Having more than one possible meaning, so that it is not clear what is intended.
words.example: Her answer was ambiguous, so nobody knew whether she had agreed.

words.def: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
words.example: With so many people leaving, some delays were inevitable.

words.def: Large in amount, size or importance.
words.example: The company made a substantial investment in new equipment.

words.def: So interesting or convincing that you cannot ignore it.
words.example: She gave a compelling argument for changing the schedule.

words.def: Causing a lot of disagreement or argument among people.
words.example: The decision to close the library was highly controversial.

words.def: Able to recover quickly after difficulties.
words.example: Children are often more resilient than adults expect.

words.def: To make something weaker or less effective, often slowly.
words.example: Constant criticism can undermine a person's confidence.

words.def: Dealing with problems in a practical, realistic way rather than following ideas or theories.
words.example: We took a pragmatic approach and fixed the most urgent problems first.

words.def: Clear, logical and easy to follow.
words.example: His speech was coherent, with each point leading naturally to the next.

words.def: Careful and detailed examination of something.
words.example: The new law came under close scrutiny from journalists.

words.def: A small, subtle difference in meaning, tone or expression.
words.example: A good translator notices nuances that a machine might miss.

words.def: Complete and careful, paying attention to every detail.
words.example: The doctor carried out a thorough examination.

words.def: Lasting for a very short time.
words.example: The beauty of cherry blossom is ephemeral, lasting only a week or two.

words.def: Seeming to be present everywhere at the same time.
words.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.

words.def: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or hidden way.
words.example: The pernicious influence of rumours slowly destroyed the team's trust.

words.def: To make something difficult to understand, often on purpose.
words.example: The report used technical language to obfuscate the real costs.

words.def: Done quickly and without real interest or care.
words.example: He gave the report a perfunctory glance and handed it back.

words.def: Refusing to obey rules or follow instructions, and difficult to control.
words.example: The recalcitrant student ignored every request to be quiet.

words.def: The luck of finding something good or valuable by chance.
words.example: Meeting my business partner at a train station was pure serendipity.

words.def: Using very few words to say something.
words.example: His laconic reply, Fine, told us nothing about how he really felt.

words.def: Appearing to be true or real, but possibly not the real reason.
words.example: The ostensible reason for the meeting was budget planning.

words.def: Done secretly or quickly so that others do not notice.
words.example: She took a surreptitious look at her phone during the lecture.

words.def: Generous and forgiving, especially towards someone you have defeated.
words.example: The winner was magnanimous and praised her opponent's effort.

words.def: A loud mixture of unpleasant sounds.
words.example: A cacophony of car horns filled the street at rush hour.
